title: Admin
lead: Read-only. Every figure here traces to a query, and nothing on this page can change anything.
readOnly: A panel that can act on data is a second application, with permissions, audit trails and a blast radius. Nothing in this one writes: a test reads every source behind it and fails on an insert, an update, a delete or a POST.

overview.activationOf: {share} of new accounts finish a round

health.title: Health
health.commitAgree: Both services are running the same commit.
health.commitDisagree: The two services are running different commits — a deploy is half-finished, or one of them failed.
health.commitUnknown: Cannot tell whether the two agree: one is down, or neither was deployed from git.
health.live: Live, whatever the range: a probe has no history.

players.title: Players
players.guests: {count, plural, =0 {no guests} one {# guest besides} other {# guests besides}}
players.ofAccounts: of {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}}
players.nobody: Nobody has finished a round yet.
players.allTimeList: All-time: rounds finished is a running total with no date on it.

activation.title: Activation
activation.activationWhy: Of the accounts created, the share that finished a round.
activation.returnWhy: Of those who finished a round, the share active on a later day.

why.created: Signed up. Guests are not counted — they are not accounts.
why.started: Pressed play at least once. Anybody missing here signed up and never began.
why.finished: Submitted at least one round. The gap above is rounds abandoned partway.
why.returned: Was active on a later day than their first. Two rounds in one sitting is not coming back.

activation.funnelLegend: share of the step above · count
activation.cameBack: {count, plural, =0 {nobody came back} one {# came back} other {# came back}}
activation.caveat: "Came back" is a later day of activity, not a cohort curve: a return the next day and a return six months on look the same here, because nothing records per-day history.
activation.cohort: The period picks who signed up, not when they played — which is what an activation figure has always meant.

games.title: Games
games.abandonWhy: Of the seats in rounds that have ended, the share whose player never submitted.
games.stillRunning: {count, plural, =0 {none still running} one {# still running} other {# still running}}
games.caveat: Only rounds that have ended count towards the rate: a seat in a round still running has not abandoned anything. And it cannot be split by screen — typing a topic, voting and waiting for generation leave no row, so the split is by mode.

traffic.title: Arrivals
traffic.reachWhy: Of the landing views in this range, the share that reached the screen with the topic field.
traffic.oneStepWhy: the one step this page is
traffic.lost: {count, plural, =0 {every landing load reached the entry screen} one {# landing load did not reach the entry screen} other {# landing loads did not reach the entry screen}}
traffic.empty: Nothing was counted in this range.
traffic.since: Counting began on {day}. A range reaching further back covers days nobody was counting, so two ranges that straddle it are not comparable.
traffic.never: Nothing has been counted yet. Arrivals are counted from the day this shipped, so an empty panel here is what a new counter looks like.
traffic.caveat: These are page loads, not people: there is no identifier anywhere in this counter, so two loads by one reader and one load by each of two readers are the same number. Reach can pass 100% — the entry screen is reachable from a bookmark without the landing.
traffic.more: {count, plural, one {# earlier day is not shown} other {# earlier days are not shown}}

cost.title: Cost
cost.noRateWhy: No token rate is configured, so this section reports tokens rather than money. Set MODEL_INPUT_COST_PER_MTOK and MODEL_OUTPUT_COST_PER_MTOK to price them — a rate written into the repository would go stale without saying so.
cost.rateSet: Priced with the configured rate per million tokens.
cost.failed: {count, plural, one {# call failed and still cost tokens} other {# calls failed and still cost tokens}}
cost.withoutTokens: {count, plural, one {# call reported no token count} other {# calls reported no token count}} — the totals above are missing them.
cost.rateIs: {input} in / {output} out per million tokens, from the two environment variables.
cost.noRateNames: No rate is configured, so this page reports tokens. Money is a multiplication a deployment opts into.
cost.generatedDenominator: {count, plural, one {# round generated} other {# rounds generated}} is what the per-round figure divides by — a cached round costs nothing to make.

content.title: Content
content.cacheWhy: A cached round costs nothing to generate, so this is what stands between a hundred rounds and a hundred generations.
content.ofGames: of {count, plural, one {# round} other {# rounds}}
content.ofCalls: of {count, plural, one {# call} other {# calls}}
content.topicFailures: {count, plural, =0 {No topic choice came back empty} one {# topic choice of {calls} came back empty} other {# topic choices of {calls} came back empty}} — a word Wikipedia has no article for is not a fault.
content.cachedOf: {cached} of {games, plural, one {# round} other {# rounds}}
content.failedOf: {failed} of {calls, plural, one {# call} other {# calls}}

range.label: Period
range.whatItMoves: The period moves the players, activation, rounds, cost and content figures. Health is a live probe, the most active list is built from running totals with no date on them, and “today” is today whatever is chosen — each says so where it appears.
range.allTime: All-time, whatever the period: these are running totals with no date on them.
range.cohort: The period picks who signed up, not when they played.

custom.title: Custom period
custom.lead: Both ends included. The period stays in the address, so it can be bookmarked and shared.
custom.days: {count, plural, one {# day selected} other {# days selected}}
custom.backwards: The first date is after the second.
